column2: On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “There are four [traits]: whoever has them is a hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he gives it up:
when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; when he disputes, he transgresses; and when he makes a covenant, he betrays it.” Recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

His words, “There are four: whoever has them is a hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he gives it up”, mean that whoever is found to have these four traits is characterised by hypocrisy in action,
and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he gives up that trait. This is part of the perfection of his ﷺ way of explaining,
for he mentions the number first and then sets out in detail what is numbered,

because that spurs the listener to be ready and prepared to take in the traits about to be imparted to him, and so that he will check himself against the number, and if it does not tally, he will know that he has missed something.
The first trait is lying in speech, that is, telling someone something in which one is lying, reporting a thing other than as it really is. In this the speaker wrongs himself
by taking on this blameworthy trait, and wrongs the one he speaks to by giving him the impression that he is truthful in what he tells him. He ﷺ said: “Hold to truthfulness,

for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise; a man keeps telling the truth and striving for truthfulness until he is written with Allah as truthful (ṣiddīq). And beware of lying,
for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire; a man keeps lying and striving for lies until he is written with Allah as a liar.” Reported by Muslim (2607).

The second trait is breaking promises, that is, making a promise while intending not to keep it. But if he makes a promise resolved to keep it, and then something arises that prevents him from keeping it, he is excused.
Abū Dāwūd (4991) reported that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿĀmir said: “My mother called me one day while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in our house,
saying: Here, come and I will give you something. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: And what did you intend to give him?
She said: I would give him some dates. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: If you had not given him anything, a lie would have been written against you.”
See al-Ṣaḥīḥah by al-Albānī (748).
The third trait is transgressing in disputes, meaning that when a person disputes with another he becomes angry and passes beyond justice into injustice. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said:

“And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just” [al-Māʾidah 5:8]; and the Exalted said: “And do not let the hatred of a people for having obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām lead you to transgress” [al-Māʾidah 5:2]. The ḥāfiẓ [Ibn Ḥajar] said in al-Fatḥ (1/90):

“Fujūr (transgression) is deviating from the truth and using stratagems to reject it.” Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (2/486): “If, in a dispute—whether about religion or worldly matters—a man has the ability to champion falsehood,

make the listener imagine it is the truth, weaken the truth and present it in the guise of falsehood, that is one of the most repugnant of forbidden things and one of the foulest traits of hypocrisy.”

The fourth trait is betrayal of covenants. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “And fulfil [every] covenant; indeed, the covenant will be questioned about” [al-Isrāʾ 17:34]; and He said: “And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, and do not break oaths after their confirmation while you have made Allah a surety over you” [al-Naḥl 16:91].
Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (2/487–488): “Betrayal is unlawful in every covenant between a Muslim and anyone else,
even if the one under covenant is a disbeliever. That is why, in the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr from the Prophet ﷺ:

‘Whoever kills a person under covenant without right will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance can be found from a distance of forty years' travel’, recorded by al-Bukhārī. Allah the Exalted has commanded in His Book that covenants with the idolaters be kept as long as they keep to their covenants and break nothing of them.

As for the covenants of Muslims among themselves, keeping them is more emphatic and breaking them a greater sin; and among the greatest of them is breaking the covenant with the ruler by one who pledged allegiance to him and accepted him.

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘There are three to whom Allah will not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and theirs is a painful punishment…’, and among them he mentioned:
‘a man who pledged allegiance to a ruler only for worldly gain; if he gives him what he wants, he keeps faith with him, and otherwise he does not keep faith with him.’

Included among the covenants that must be kept and in which betrayal is unlawful are all the contracts of Muslims among themselves to which they have agreed, such as sales, marriages and other binding contracts that must be fulfilled,
and likewise what must be fulfilled for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, of what the servant pledges to his Lord, such as a vow of devotion and the like.”
It is part of good teaching for the teacher to mention the number before explaining what is numbered,
so that it makes a deeper impression on the learner's mind.
An explanation of the danger of the traits of hypocrisy being combined in a person.
A warning against lying in speech, and that it is a trait of hypocrisy.
A warning against breaking promises, and that it is a trait of hypocrisy.
A warning against transgressing in disputes, and that it is a trait of hypocrisy.
A warning against betraying covenants, and that it is a trait of hypocrisy.
